REASON FOR RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN RESUBMISSION AND UPDATE

Stolthaven Houston, Inc. is updating the facility's Risk Management Plan ("RMP") in May of 2025 as a result of planned changes involving Acrylonitrile storage and handling in an existing Covered Process at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal, and the addition of a new Covered Process for transloading of Pentanes.  

The specific changes associated with this RMP update include:

- Adding Acrylonitrile storage in Internal Floating Roof ("IFR") Storage Tank P15-40 above the Threshold Quantity, and associated Acrylonitrile handling, in the existing in P-Tank Farm Covered Process at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal.   P-Tank Farm is an existing Covered Process due to the ongoing storage of Vinyl Acetate Monomer ("VAM").  

- Adding a new Covered Process for Isopentane , n-Pentane, and Mixed Pentanes (5-95-percent) transloading directly between rail cars located at Spots 1 and 2 of Rail Rack R-5 and ISO tank containers spotted at Truck Rack T-8 with no intermediate on-site storage in an above-ground tank.  Note that Stolthaven Houston has successfully performed transloading between rail cars and ISO tank containers of Isopentane , n-Pentane, and Mixed Pentanes between Rail Rack R-2 and Truck Rack T-6 in a separate Covered Process regulated under the RMP for over 18-years.  

- Updating the off-site consequence analyses ("OCA") for all Covered Processes based on current Environmental Protection Agency ("EPA") guidance related to release temperatures. 

- Providing new Worst Case Release Scenarios for toxics (Acrylonitrile in Tank P15-40) and flammables, noting that all four flammable release scenarios have the same radius of impact.

- Providing new Alternate Case Release Scenarios for all three regulated toxics and one flammable, noting that all four flammable release scenarios have the same radius of impact.  

- Various data element updates since the previous RMP update and certification in November of 2024.  


§ 68.1

55(a):  ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICIES

Stolthaven Houston, Inc. is committed to operating and maintaining our processes related to bulk chemical storage and distribution in a safe and responsible manner.  The facility uses a combination of accidental release prevention and emergency response planning programs to protect the environment and to ensure the safety of our employees and assets, our industrial neighbors, and the citizens of the surrounding community.  This Executive Summary provides a brief overview of the comprehensive risk management activities that Stolthaven Houston, Inc. has designed and implemented, including:

- A description of our facility and the substances regulated by 40 CFR 68 that may be handled on-site in stationary sources above their corresponding Threshold Quantities.

- An overview of our accidental release prevention programs.

- A five-year history of significant accidental releases, if applicable, from processes covered by the United States EPA RMP regulations.

- An overview of our emergency response programs.

- An overview of completed and planned improvements at the facility to help prevent accidental chemical releases from occurring, and

- Detailed information about our RMP.


§ 68.155(b):  STATIONARY SOURCES AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES HANDLED

Stolthaven Houston, Inc. owns and operates a bulk liquids storage and distribution terminal located on the north side of the Houston Ship Channel near Channelview in eastern Harris County, Texas.  The facility currently consists of 188 above-ground "for-hire" storage tanks that vary in capacity from 2,000-barrels up to 110,000-barrels, five truck loading/unloading racks (Truck Racks T-3, T-4, T-5, T-6, and T-8), four rail car loading/unloading racks (Rail Racks R-1, R-2, R-3, and R-5), one dedicated barge dock (Barge Dock-C), a finger pier jetty equipped with two separate marine vessel berths for handling barges and ships (Dock 2/3), and a jetty placed into s

ervice in 2019 for handling barges and ships (Dock 11).  A rail car cleaning and intermodal transfer station (Rail Rack R-4 and Truck Rack T-7) is also located within the Stolthaven Houston Terminal, and a biological waste water treatment plant and various air pollution control devices are operated on-site to reduce the impact of the Stolthaven Houston Terminal's operations on the environment.  Stolthaven Houston has an ongoing capital expansion project that will add 13 additional low-pressure storage tanks, and associated infrastructure at the facility, between the third-quarter of 2025 and into 2026.  

Bulk liquid products are received into the Stolthaven Houston Terminal by various modes of transportation cargo container including tank trucks, ISO tank containers, flexi-bags, rail tank cars, barges, and marine parcel tankers.  The received liquid products are stored on-site according to customer-specified requirements, and are subsequently transferred off-site through one or more of the above-referenced transportation modes.  Stolthaven Houston, Inc. also performs direct product transfers between marine vessels and rail tank cars with no intermediate storage in the facility's above-ground storage tanks.  Similarly, land-based intermodal transfers directly between tank trucks, ISO tank containers, flexi-bags, and rail tank cars are also performed routinely at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal.  Note that Stolthaven Houston, Inc. does not perform any chemical processing or chemical manufacturing operations on-site, and the company does not own nor ultimately control the disposition of the various bulk liquid products that are stored or otherwise handled at the facility.

The following chemicals handled at Stolthaven Houston, Inc. are identified by the EPA as having the potential to cause adverse off-site consequences in the event of a significant accidental release:

Regulated Toxic Substances Currently in Storage:

Toluene Diisocyanate, Mixed Isomers: Chemical Abst

racts Service ("CAS") Number 26471-62-5
Vinyl Acetate Monomer: CAS Number 108-05-4
Acrylonitrile: CAS Number 107-13-1

Regulated Flammable Substances Handled via Intermodal Transfers (Loaded Rail Cars into Empty ISO Tank Containers):

Isopentane: CAS Number 78-78-4
n-Pentane:  CAS Number 109-66-0
Pentane Blends (5-95% Isopentane and n-Pentane Mixtures)

TDI, VAM, and Acrylonitrile currently represent the only three RMP regulated substances at Stolthaven Houston, Inc. that are present on-site above their corresponding Threshold Quantities at all times.  Isopentane, n-Pentane, and Pentane Blends consisting of between 5 and 95-percent Isopentane and n-Pentane are periodically transloaded directly from loaded rail tank cars into empty ISO tank containers with no intermediate on-site storage, other than loaded rail cars received into the facility that are staged on the terminal's rail car storage tracks prior to performing the cargo transfer operation.  Accordingly, Isopentane and n-Pentane are not always present above their respective Threshold Quantities at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal.  As such, the "Predictive Filing" option in Section 1 (Registration Information), Item 1.16, of this RMP is noted as "Y".   

Our training and accidental release prevention programs in combination with our Standard Operating Procedures ("SOP") and contingency planning efforts help us effectively manage potential hazards posed to our employees, the public, and the environment during the storage and/or transfer of the above-referenced RMP regulated substances.

ISOPENTANE, N-PENTANE, & PENTANE BLEND INTERMODAL TRANSFERS BETWEEN R-5 & T-8: PROCESS 1

In May of 2025 Stolthaven Houston is adding the operational flexibility to periodically transload Isopentane, n-Pentane, and Pentane Blends directly between loaded rail tank cars spotted at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal's Rail Rack R-5 into empty ISO tank containers located at Truck Rack T-8, with no intermediate product storage in any of

the terminal's above-ground storage tanks.  Vapors generated during these intermittent cargo transfer operations would be directed to the East Property Vapor Combustor (VC-TCE) for emission control.  As noted below for Process 3, Stolthaven Houston has successfully performed similar transloading operations for Pentanes between Rail Rack R-2 and Truck Rack T-6 for over 18-years.  In an effort to reduce congestion from heavy operational activity at the facility's Truck Rack T-6, Stolthaven Houston proposes the option to also perform transloading for loaded Pentane (Iso, Normal, and Blends) rail cars into empty ISO tank containers between Rail Rack R-5 and Truck Rack T-8 using the dedicated R5-T8-143 transfer line, which has automated control valves installed at both the truck rack and the rail rack.   Operationally the Pentane transloading operations between rail cars and ISO tank containers are identical, except for the location of the activity within the Stolthaven Houston Terminal, and the corresponding vapor control device.  

Loaded pentane rail cars are received into the Stolthaven Houston Terminal, and will be held on the facility's rail storage tracks before being moved to Rail Rack R-5 to perform the product transfers into empty ISO Tank Containers that have been pre-purged with Nitrogen and spotted at Truck Rack T-8.  Note that after loading, the ISO Containers are secured, weighed, and immediately shipped off-site by tractor-trailer after the appropriate transportation paperwork is completed.  Maximum chemical inventories reported with this RMP for Isopentane and n-Pentane conservatively assume that 12 rail cars loaded with 31,500-gallons of Isopentane cargo and six rail cars loaded with 31,500-gallons of n-Pentane cargo are held simultaneously on the facility's storage tracks.   Rail cars of the blended Pentane mixture are included in these totals.  During calendar year 2024, 86 separate Isopentane and n-Pentane intermodal transfer events were completed a

t the Stolthaven Houston Terminal between Racks R-2 and T-6 under existing Covered Process 3.   As of the May 2025 RMP update Stolthaven Houston does not have a definitive date to commence Pentane transloading between Racks R-5 and T-8, as this operational activity remains ongoing at Racks R-2 and T-6 as described below.  


D-TANK FARM TOLUENE DIISOCYANATE STORAGE AND TRANSFERS: PROCESS 2

Stolthaven Houston, Inc. currently stores TDI in two 15,000-barrel nominal capacity above-ground storage tanks (Low-Pressure Storage Tanks D15-19 and D15-22).  Tank D15-19, which represents the facility's largest volume of TDI held in a single storage vessel, has a maximum TDI storage capacity of approximately 6.3-million pounds (617,718-gallons), and Tank D15-22 has a maximum TDI storage capacity of approximately 6.2-million pounds (610,729-gallons).  TDI is received into the facility via delivery by marine parcel tankers, tank trucks, and rail tank cars; TDI is shipped outbound from Stolthaven Houston, Inc. by rail tank cars and marine parcel tankers.  Periodic direct transfers of TDI from marine vessels into rail tank cars is also performed at Stolthaven Houston, Inc. with no intermediate product storage in the two referenced D-Tank Farm low-pressure storage tanks.  Note that Stolthaven Houston, Inc. has over 30-years' experience in the safe storage and handling of TDI. 

As part of the changes associated with additional TDI storage in Low-Pressure Storage Tank D15-19 (Stolthaven Houston's most recent TDI expansion project), significant modifications were performed such that TDI is handled safely and efficiently in this tank, including installing a liner on the storage tank's floor and shell, installing a pipeline constructed of 316L stainless steel from the storage tank to the existing dock line in D-Manifold used exclusively for TDI marine-based transfers, replacing all existing gate valves on the Tank D15-19 system with ball valves for ease of operation and automation capab

ility using pneumatic actuators, installing a stainless-steel pump for TDI at Storage Tank D15-19, installing hot water external heating panels, a water tank, and associated heating panel supply/return lines for Storage Tank D15-19 while in TDI service, insulating Tank D15-19, installing internal eductors at the tank's recirculation line to improve product mixing, installing electric heat tracing and insulation on the tank's lateral pipeline to D-Manifold, installing a dehydrator on the tank's vacuum breaker to help prevent moisture from entering the vapor space should there be a loss of plant nitrogen, and installing a carbon adsorption canister on the Storage Tank D15-19 vapor line prior to TDI vapors entering the terminal's common Tank Farm Vent Flare vapor header to reduce the concentration of TDI in the vapor system.  Full automation for D-Tank Farm has been completed, which provides pump controls, valve controls, and automatic overfill protection for storage tanks and transportation containers while transferring cargo to and from this tank farm.  


ISOPENTANE, N-PENTANE, & PENTANE BLEND INTERMODAL TRANSFERS BETWEEN R-2 & T-6: PROCESS 3

Isopentane, n-Pentane, and Pentane Blends containing a 5 to 95-percent mixture of Isopentane and n-Pentane are periodically transloaded directly between loaded rail tank cars spotted at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal's Rail Rack R-2 into empty ISO tank containers located at Truck Rack T-6, with no intermediate product storage in any of the terminal's above-ground storage tanks.  Vapors generated during these intermittent transfer operations are directed to the Tank Farm Vent Flare for emission control.  Loaded pentane rail cars are received into the Stolthaven Houston Terminal, and are held on the facility's rail storage tracks before being moved to Rail Rack R-2 to perform the product transfers into empty ISO Tank Containers that have been pre-purged with Nitrogen and spotted at Truck Rack T-6.  Note that after loading, the

ISO Containers are secured, weighed, and immediately shipped off-site by tractor-trailer after the appropriate transportation paperwork is completed.  Maximum chemical inventories reported with this RMP for Isopentane and n-Pentane conservatively assume that 12 rail cars loaded with 31,500-gallons of Isopentane cargo and six rail cars loaded with 31,500-gallons of n-Pentane cargo are held simultaneously on the facility's storage tracks.   Rail cars of the blended Pentane mixture are included in these totals.  During calendar year 2024, 86 separate Isopentane and n-Pentane intermodal transfer events were completed at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal between Racks R-2 and T-6.  Note that all Isopentane, n-Pentane, and Pentane Blend intermodal transfers between Rack R-2 and Rack T-6 use the same equipment and transfer spots.  A dedicated transfer line between Rail Rack R-2 and Truck Rack T-6 through G-Manifold (the R2-T6-70 Line) is used for this Covered Process transloading operation.  Only one Pentane rail car is unloaded at a time.  


P-TANK FARM VINYL ACETATE MONOMER AND ACRYLONITRILE (REGULATED TOXIC SUBSTANCES) STORAGE AND TRANSFERS: PROCESS 4

Storage Tank P50-5 is an existing IFR tank at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal with a maximum working capacity of 50,445-barrels, which corresponds to a maximum VAM storage capacity of approximately 16.6-million pounds (2,118,691-gallons).  Tank P50-5, which represents the facility's largest volume of VAM held in a single storage vessel, was placed into VAM service for the first time on February 25, 2010.  VAM is received into this tank via barge delivery using a dedicated marine dock line.  Product is stored and subsequently shipped outbound according to customer requirements via marine parcel tankers, and occasionally by barges, that load at Stolthaven Houston's existing Dock 2/3.  VAM may also be transferred periodically directly from barges into rail tank cars with no intermediate product storage, directly between barge

s and marine parcel tankers using a shore loop dock line, and VAM slops can also be received into the terminal from marine vessels berthed at Stolthaven Houston's docks.    Vapors generated during all VAM loading operations are controlled by a Vapor Combustor, and a quarterly leak detection and repair ("LDAR") program is applied to find and promptly repair any equipment leaks.  

In 2017 Stolthaven Houston placed IFR Storage Tank P50-4 into VAM service.  Tank P50-4 has a working capacity of 48,651-barrels, which corresponds to a maximum VAM storage capacity of approximately 16-million pounds (2,043,337-gallons).  As a result of the 2017 VAM storage project for Tank P50-4, piping modifications were completed in P-Manifold to connect the marine transfer system for Tank P50-4 into the existing Dock Line P-D3-78, which was already in place for Tank P50-5 and is dedicated exclusively to VAM service.  A new VAM filter-pot was also installed adjacent to Storage Tank P50-4.  

Stolthaven Houston's permanent, stationary fire-water protection systems in the immediate area of Tank P50-5 were also upgraded to provide additional cooling water if-needed in the event of an emergency incident involving any of the facility's flammable or combustible liquid storage tanks in close proximity.  Existing portable water delivery systems also remain available should they be needed in the event of an emergency.  Note that Stolthaven Houston, Inc. has over 15-years' experience in the safe storage and handling of VAM.  Stolthaven Houston plans to fully automate P-Tank Farm under a capital project that will begin in 2025.   Quick close ball valves equipped with remote actuators were installed on both P-Tank Farm VAM storage tanks when these two tanks were last clean and empty in anticipation of installing full automation controls beginning in 2025 with a 2026 completion date.  

Stolthaven Houston plans to place IFR Storage Tank P15-40 into Acrylonitrile service for the first time in May of 20

25 as part of the existing P-Tank Farm Covered Process.  Tank P15-40 has a working capacity of 15,219-barrels, which corresponds to a maximum Acrylonitrile storage capacity of approximately 4.3-million pounds (639,210-gallons).   Existing Marine Dock Lines P-C3-62, C3-D3-62, and C3-D3-62 will be dedicated exclusively to Acrylonitrile service.   

Stolthaven Houston will receive Acrylonitrile into Tank P15-40 via inbound marine deliveries from barges and parcel tankers.  The cargo will be stored, and ultimately transferred off-site via trucks loaded at Truck Rack T-6, rail cars loaded at Rail Rack R-2, and barges and ships loaded at Dock 2/3.  Vapors generated during all Acrylonitrile loading operations will be controlled by either a flare (trucks and rail cars) or a Vapor Combustor (barges and ships), and a quarterly LDAR program will be applied to find and promptly repair any equipment leaks.   IFR Storage Tank P15-40 is equipped with an independent local high-level alarm in the field, in addition to continuous tank level monitoring in the Stolthaven Houston operations control room.  End of line valve controls at Dock 2/3, Truck Rack T-6, and Rail Rack R-2 are currently automated for Storage Tank P15-40.  Stolthaven Houston plans to fully automate P-Tank Farm under a capital project that will begin in 2025 with a 2026 completion date.  

The Acrylonitrile cargo held in Tank P15-40 will be inhibited before delivery to the Stolthaven Houston Terminal for quality control reasons.  


Q-TANK FARM VINYL ACETATE MONOMER STORAGE AND TRANSFERS: PROCESS 5

On November 27, 2024 Stolthaven Houston placed IFR Storage Tank Q30-13 into VAM service for the first time in a newly Covered Process.  Tank Q30-13 has a working capacity of 30,707-barrels, which corresponds to a maximum VAM storage capacity of approximately 10-million pounds (1,289,684-gallons).   Existing Marine Dock Line A6-D3-89 to Dock 2/3, which was already in place for Storage Tank Q30-13, is dedicated exclusively

to VAM service for this Covered Process.   

Stolthaven Houston receives VAM into Tank Q30-13 via inbound marine deliveries from barges and parcel tankers.  The cargo is stored, and ultimately transferred off-site, via trucks loaded at Truck Rack T-4, rail cars loaded at Rail Rack R-3, and barges and ships loaded at Dock 2/3.  Vapors generated during all VAM loading operations are controlled by a Vapor Combustor, and a quarterly LDAR program is applied to find and promptly repair any equipment leaks.   IFR Storage Tank Q30-13 is equipped with an independent high-level alarm in the field, in addition to continuous tank level monitoring in the Stolthaven Houston operations control room.  

The VAM in Tank Q30-13 is inhibited for quality control reasons.  A third-party surveyor samples the tank on a monthly basis to verify inhibitor levels, and adds inhibitor as necessary to ensure the tank remains on specification.  After inhibitor is added the tank is circulated to ensure adequate mixing.  

Tank pump control and end of line valve controls at Dock 2/3 and Truck Rack T-4 are currently automated for Storage Tank Q30-13.  Stolthaven Houston installed a valve that can be operated remotely on the Storage Tank Q30-13 rail system located at Rack R-3 in 2024 to provide for future full automation of rail system operations.  Stolthaven Houston plans to fully automate Q-Tank Farm under a capital project that will begin in 2026.   Quick close ball valves that may be equipped with remote actuators were installed at Tank Q30-13 when this tank was previously clean and empty in anticipation of installing full automation controls by 2027.  

For the purpose of defining maximum chemical inventories noted in this RMP, the densities of all regulated substances at their lowest expected operating temperatures were chosen to provide conservative estimates for the maximum chemical quantities (in pounds) that may be on-site at one time.  For the OCA parameters, specifically the vapor pressur

es for each regulated substance, Stolthaven Houston applied the vapor pressures at maximum temperatures according to current EPA guidance to provide the most conservative OCA modeling results.  

   
§ 68.155(c):  ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM

We take a systematic, proactive approach to prevent accidental releases of chemicals at Stolthaven Houston.  Our management systems address each of the key features of successful prevention programs, including:

- Process Safety Information ("PSI")

- Process Hazard Analysis ("PHA")

- ISO 9001:2015 Certified Quality Management System ("QMS") for continuous process improvement

- Employee Training / Local Training Manual 

- Mechanical Integrity

- Spill Containment, Control, and Countermeasures

- Management of Change ("MOC")

- Pre-Startup Safety Review ("PSSR")

- Vapor Control Systems

- Compliance Audits

- Formal Incident Investigation

- Employee Participation Program

- Hot Work / Safe Work Permits

- Departmental / Safety Meetings

- Trained Emergency Response Team ("ERT")

- Emergency / Incident Response Contractors

- Mutual Aid Membership and North Channel Area LEPC

- Ongoing Automation Enhancements and Upgrades

The above-referenced elements of our prevention program work together to help us prevent and respond, as needed, to any accidental chemical releases.  Our company and our employees are committed to the standard these management systems set for the way we conduct business, and we have controls in place to ensure that we meet our own high standards for accident prevention.


§ 68.155(d):  FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY

During the preceding five years there have been no accidental releases from any RMP covered process at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal that resulted in deaths, injuries, significant property damage on site, or known offsite deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering-in-place, property damage, or environmental damage. 

All incidents at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal are formally investi

gated as part of our facility's ISO Certified QMS to identify the root cause of the event, and to implement appropriate corrective actions for continuous process improvement.


§ 68.155(e):  EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

We maintain an integrated contingency plan, which consolidates the various federal, state, and local regulatory requirements for emergency response planning.  Stolthaven Houston maintains a Facility Response Plan ("FRP") with the United States Coast Guard, Houston-Galveston Sector. Our emergency response program provides the essential planning and training standards for effectively protecting our employees, the public, the environment, and company assets during potential emergency situations.  Furthermore, we coordinate our action plan with the community emergency response plan and the North Channel Area Local Emergency Planning Committee ("LEPC").  Stolthaven Houston's hazardous chemical inventory report (i.e. Tier II report) is maintained current with the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality ("TCEQ"), the North Channel Area LEPC, and the local Channelview, Texas Fire Department.  Stolthaven Houston, Inc. is also a member of Channel Industries Mutual Aid ("CIMA"), which can provide world-class, rapid response assistance in the event of an on-site emergency.    

An Emergency Action Plan ("EAP") is maintained which provides guidelines for responding to various emergencies such as fires, hazardous material spills, personnel injuries, severe weather events, and property damage that may occur at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal.   


§ 68.155(f):  CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY

The following is a list of completed and planned/ongoing initiatives at the Stolthaven Houston Terminal to assist in preventing and/or responding to accidental chemical releases, to protect company employees and the environment, and to effectively manage hazards present at the facility:

- As they are made available when empty and clean, cargo tanks are equipped with quick-closing

ball valves to replace existing gate valves as part of ongoing safety enhancements and automation efforts, which include status alarms displayed in the terminal's 24-hour Operations Control Room, automated tank overfill protection systems, pump controls, and remotely actuated valve closures.  Complete automation of D-Tank Farm and associated systems has been completed.  Automation of P-Tank Farm and associated systems is planned to commence in 2025 and be completed in 2026.   Automation of Q-Tank Farm and associated systems is planned to commence in 2026 and be completed in 2027.

- Tank Farms A, AE, and BE, while not currently covered by the EPA RMP regulations, are fully automated, as will be new Tank Farms CE and DE, which are under construction and are expected to become operational during late 2025 and early 2026.  

- Automated end-of-line valves installed at Truck Racks, Rail Racks, and Marine Docks to assist in preventing overfills and possible cargo contaminations.  

- Double verification of all line and hose connections before commencing any product transfer operations to reduce the possibility of incorrect valve and/or hose alignment.

- Added a concrete secondary containment floor and total organic carbon ("TOC") analyzer to the facility's A-Tank Farm.  A-Tank Farm is one of Stolthaven Houston's original Tank Farms, and was originally constructed with earthen secondary containment.  

- New fire monitor and valve installation in A-Tank Farm that provides 500 to 1000-gallons per minute ("GPM") water flow.  

- Purchased a Ferrara Inferno Super Pumper Fire Truck, which can provide 6,000-GPM of flow; the truck holds 800-gallons of fire-fighting foam and 200-gallons of water.  

- Security camera upgrades improving video coverage at the facility's truck loading racks and piping manifolds.  

- Continuous improvement through the facility's ISO 9001:2015 Certified QMS.

- Employee Experienced Feedback Program.

- Two 753-horsepower fire-water pump driver eme

rgency diesel engines added at Ship Dock 11 for fire-fighting response.  

- Gas detection systems updated to include 5-gas monitors with photo-ionization detectors ("PID").

- Live fire school training at Texas A&M University for Stolthaven Houston ERT members, where they progress from basic training to become advanced fire fighters.  

- Additional emergency response training for facility management personnel.

- Contractor evaluation performed by a third-party service.
